conventions.convention: Spatial translations relabel configuration-basis sites by x; τ₀ is the identity and τₓ₊ᵧ=τₓ∘τᵧ. Interaction shapes are anchored with lexicographically least site 0, and each nonzero translation orbit is represented once.
Finite-volume Hamiltonians use free boundaries: include exactly interaction terms whose complete support lies in the region. The trace is the ordinary, unnormalized finite-matrix trace.

A van Hove sequence consists of finite nonempty regions with volumes tending to infinity and inner-boundary fractions tending to zero for every fixed integer width r≥0, using the max-coordinate lattice distance. Cube sides are positive integers.
β>0 is inverse energy; p is dimensionless log-partition per site, and free energy per site is −β⁻¹p. Energy concentration is centered at eΦ(β)=−pΦ′(β), assuming differentiability at β.

Entropy density is dimensionless, with 0 log 0=0, and is taken along Q_L={0,…,L−1}^d. Stationary means invariance under every spatial translation, rather than invariance under time evolution. Countable Choice and full Choice are explicitly assumed for the stated supplier chains.
The stationary variational maximum does not identify its maximizing states with KMS states and makes no empirical material claim.

load_bearing.statement: For a translation-invariant uniformly bounded finite-range interaction and fixed β>0, pΛₙ(β) converges to the same finite pΦ(β) along every van Hove sequence. Every sequence of self-adjoint Bₙ on those volumes with ‖Bₙ‖/|Λₙ|→0 leaves that limit unchanged.

A uniformly bounded finite-range interaction is translation invariant when τₓ(Φ(Z))=Φ(Z+x) for every finite nonempty support Z and every x∈ℤ^d; its finite anchored-shape list represents each nonzero translation orbit once.

Under the stated Countable Choice, Choice, finite-entropy and compactness inputs, every translation-invariant algebraic state has cube entropy density equal to the infimum of normalized cube entropies and energy density uΦ(ω)=ΣS ω(Φ(S)); the invariant state space is sequentially compact for pointwise convergence, entropy density is upper semicontinuous, and energy density is continuous.

Under its stated finite-range translation-invariant model, β>0, k_B>0, choice assumptions and finite-dimensional/state-extension interfaces, pΦ(β)=maxω∈Sinv(s(ω)−βuΦ(ω)), and at least one maximizing state exists.

concerns.concern: The Statement says “For each finite region Λ” and then defines mΛ,β:=|Λ|⁻¹ TrΛ(ρΛ,β HΛ). The prerequisite def-qsm-local-spin-algebras explicitly permits Λ=∅ and assigns its Hilbert space dimension one. For that region H∅=0 and Z∅=1, but the displayed mean energy density divides by zero. Restrict this definition to finite nonempty regions. The van Hove conclusion already has that restriction and its concentration proof is unaffected.

seams_checked.note: The thermodynamic-limit page uses the earlier bounded finite-range interaction definition at its exact self-adjointness, finite-range, per-site norm and free-boundary scope, then adds translation invariance. Its pressure proof does not invoke a stronger dynamical limit or an infinite-volume Hamiltonian.

The coexistence theorem uses the translation automorphisms from def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction to transfer spatial stationarity through the diagonal lift. Its relabeling identity agrees with the supplier's translation direction. Its pressure-cusp argument uses separate CSM suppliers and does not infer KMS–variational equivalence from this batch.

The physical-quantities definition retains the precise inner-boundary van Hove condition, dimensionless pressure normalization, entropy convention and explicit choice assumptions. The equilibrium-predictions theorem applies the pressure result only after adding translation invariance, retains β>0 and free boundaries, and distinguishes model deductions from empirical claims and mechanical pressure.
